settings.label: Client ID
settings.meaning: Names the app's REST API app. The server signs in with it, and the browser's PayPal JavaScript SDK loads with it.
settings.whereToFind: Developer Dashboard › Apps & Credentials, in the app's REST API credentials. Use the Sandbox/Live toggle at the top: test uses the sandbox app's, production the live app's. Nothing in the value tells the two apart.

settings.label: Client secret
settings.meaning: Authenticates the client ID when the server asks PayPal for an access token (OAuth 2.0 client credentials).
settings.whereToFind: Developer Dashboard › Apps & Credentials, next to the client ID of the same app and environment (Sandbox/Live toggle).

settings.label: Environment
settings.meaning: Which PayPal the credentials belong to: sandbox calls api-m.sandbox.paypal.com, live calls api-m.paypal.com. PayPal's credentials carry no prefix, so this says it.
settings.whereToFind: sandbox or live: the side of the Sandbox/Live toggle the credentials were copied from.

test.because: Test runs against PayPal's sandbox: set PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT=sandbox with the sandbox app's credentials

production.because: Production takes real payments: set PAYPAL_ENVIRONMENT=live with the live app's credentials

settings.label: Webhook ID
settings.meaning: The webhook PayPal signs each delivery for. Not a secret, but a delivery only verifies with it, so it's required to receive webhooks.
settings.whereToFind: Developer Dashboard › Apps & Credentials › the app › Webhooks, after adding the app's webhook URL. Sandbox and live apps each have their own.

operations.name: oauth.token
operations.purpose: Exchanges the client ID and secret for an access token (client credentials, HTTP Basic). Cached until shortly before it expires.

operations.name: orders.create
operations.purpose: Creates an order to capture one payment. The buyer approves it on PayPal (the JavaScript SDK, or the order's approve link) before it can be captured.

operations.name: orders.get
operations.purpose: Reads an order: its status, purchase unit and any captures and refunds.

operations.name: orders.capture
operations.purpose: Captures the payment of an order the buyer approved.

operations.name: captures.get
operations.purpose: Reads a captured payment, with the order it belongs to.

operations.name: captures.refund
operations.purpose: Refunds a captured payment, in full or in part.

operations.name: refunds.get
operations.purpose: Reads a refund.

operations.name: sales.get
operations.purpose: Reads a subscription payment (a sale), with the subscription it paid for.

operations.name: saleRefunds.get
operations.purpose: Reads a refund of a subscription payment.

operations.name: products.create
operations.purpose: Creates a catalog product, which billing plans belong to.

operations.name: products.list
operations.purpose: Lists catalog products, a page at a time.

operations.name: plans.create
operations.purpose: Creates a billing plan for a product: its price and how often it bills.

operations.name: plans.list
operations.purpose: Lists billing plans, a page at a time, optionally of one product.

operations.name: plans.get
operations.purpose: Reads a billing plan with its billing cycles.

operations.name: subscriptions.create
operations.purpose: Creates a subscription to a plan. It waits for the subscriber to approve it on PayPal (its approve link, or the JavaScript SDK) before it becomes active.

operations.name: subscriptions.get
operations.purpose: Reads a subscription: its status, plan, quantity and billing info.

operations.name: subscriptions.suspend
operations.purpose: Suspends a subscription: it stops billing until it is activated again.

operations.name: subscriptions.activate
operations.purpose: Activates a suspended subscription.

operations.name: subscriptions.cancel
operations.purpose: Cancels a subscription, at once.

operations.name: subscriptions.revise
operations.purpose: Asks to change a subscription's plan or quantity. The subscriber approves the change on PayPal, through the approve link in the answer.

operations.name: webhookCerts.get
operations.purpose: Downloads the X.509 certificate a webhook delivery names in PAYPAL-CERT-URL, to check its signature. Only from PayPal's own API host.

signature.description: PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-SIG is the base64 RSA signature (PAYPAL-AUTH-ALGO: SHA256withRSA) of the string <PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-ID>|<PAYPAL-TRANSMISSION-TIME>|<webhook id>|<CRC32 of the raw body, as an unsigned decimal>, made with the key of the X.509 certificate at PAYPAL-CERT-URL. The webhook id is not sent: it is the one the app's webhook was given. Fetch the certificate only from PayPal's API host for the environment (https, /v1/notifications/certs/<id>), and cache it. The body is covered only by its CRC32, so re-read the resource from the API before acting on money. PayPal retries a delivery that isn't answered 2xx, up to 25 times over 3 days.

events.meaning: A merchant refunds a payment capture.
A merchant refunds a subscription payment.
A subscription payment is reversed (a chargeback, or a payment PayPal takes back).
